cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've closed the flight page like you. Booking finished. Except I haven't bought our anniversary tickets. Can you stay while I explain?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I closed a duplicate tab. I thought you needed help finding a flight.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, one page at a time. I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I find the words?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 says booking finished then immediately admits it is not, weakening never-admit-confusion; A3 and A5 progressively risk real emotional truth.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 duplicate correction supports A3 page cover; B4 trip-or-us causes A5 deeper admission. A1 finished/not-bought is the local conflict.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers flights help and B4 stays with difficult subject.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 supportive question to reveal relationship doubt.

specificity.evidence: A1 anniversary/laptop and B2 duplicate explain setting.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 find-the-words request is purposeful vulnerability.
